Feature Importance & Error by Rating Value
Which features drive predictions most + where each model struggles
🏆 Why SVD Won
SVD (Collaborative Filtering) outperformed all regression models because it understands latent user-movie relationships. It captures hidden patterns like "users who love Sci-Fi also rate Animation highly" — something regression models can't see. RMSE of 0.35 stars means predictions are off by less than half a star on average.
📊 Baseline Reality Check
The Baseline model (predicting the global mean of 3.64 for every movie) achieved RMSE of 0.74 — more than double SVD's error. R² of -0.003 means it explains zero variance. This is our benchmark — any real model must beat this significantly, and all 4 did.
🎬 Top Performing Genre
Animation movies received the highest average ratings (4.12★) while Horror received the lowest. This aligns with real-world MovieLens data where family-friendly content scores high due to broader appeal. Recommendation: promote Animation titles to undecided users as a safe bet.
👤 Key Prediction Features
The most important features for Random Forest were movie_mean (average rating of the movie) and user_mean (user's average rating bias). This confirms both item popularity and user behavior are the strongest signals for rating prediction — not demographics.
